title: Lesson 2 - Modeling design considerations: normalized vs denormalized, standard vs custom, common data model
description: Compare and contrast normalization and denormalization, standard versus custom object use, and the Salesforce common data model (accounts, contacts, person accounts, and the object relationships that underpin Customer 360) so you can choose the right design trade-off for a customer scenario.

questions.question: A reporting team complains that each sales report requires five lookup hops to reach a stable 'Region' value that never changes. What is the best architectural recommendation?
options: Normalize further by creating a shared Region object referenced by all parties
Denormalize Region onto the transactional object as a stored or formula-derived field
Move the value to a Big Object for fast retrieval
Replace the lookup with a polymorphic relationship
questions.explanation: Stable reference values are prime denormalization candidates; more normalization adds hops (A), Big Objects are for volume not for a single stable value (C), and polymorphic lookups do not simplify reporting (D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Person Accounts are TRUE?
options: They are ideal when modeling individual consumers alongside business accounts
Enablement can be toggled on and off per record type
They pair a single Account and Contact record for the same person
Enablement is org-wide and effectively irreversible
questions.explanation: Person Accounts suit B2C individual modeling (A) and are org-wide/irreversible (D); they are not toggled per record type (B false), and the pairing statement (C) is true as a fact but the question asks for the scenario-relevant pair - A and D capture the design trade-off.

questions.question: An integration must map four source systems onto Salesforce. Which artifact should the architect produce FIRST to keep the mapping consistent?
options: A page layout per source system
A canonical common data model mapping source fields to target objects
A set of validation rules per system
A separate custom object per source system
questions.explanation: A common data model is the prerequisite for consistent multi-source mapping; page layouts (A), validation (C) and per-system objects (D) are downstream or fragmenting choices.
